chunks.content: 96 How Skipping a Lawyer Cost This Buyer Big Time (Don’t Be Like John) Hi Sara, Let me tell you about John. John bought an accounting practice. He thought he did his homework – checked the books, met the clients, even pictured himself finally taking an Alaskan cruise with his wife after tax season. What he didn’t do? Hire a lawyer. Big mistake. Turns out, the previous owner had been fabricating write-offs for clients. After the sale closed, John had to spend hours—with every single client—breaking the bad news. Clients were furious, some left, and John was stuck paying off a 10-year SBA loan for a practice that was now hemorrhaging revenue. All because he skipped legal counsel. Here’s what a lawyer would have done for john: Helped him structure his deal with greater retention mechanics so he could ensure the Seller kept some skin in the game Added protections in the purchase agreement (like warranties and indemnities) to shield him from the fallout of past misdeeds Instead, John was left footing the bill—both financially and emotionally. Don't be like John. When you’re buying an accounting practice (or any business, really), you need more than Google and good intentions. You need a lawyer who knows the deal landscape—someone who can: Draft a purchase agreement that actually protects you Ensure you’re not inheriting someone else’s mess and that you have solutions to help if you do The cost of hiring an attorney? A fraction of what John lost trying to fix someone else’s mistakes. Thinking of buying a firm? Let’s make sure your success story doesn’t start like John’s. To smart deals (and zero client write-off scandals), Sara Sharp Partner, SK&S Law Group Business Consultant & Founder, Deal Academy P.S.
